The initial entity-slot limit is 3. $186D copies it to $4DBA, which bounds the slots that entity records fill: the initializer at $1863 loads records into slots 1 to 3 ($18CB). The load has 5 entity records, so the initializer stops at the limit with records 4–5 left; each pass, the slot scan at $3622 checks slots 1 to 3 ($3629), and $3632 gives an empty slot the next record (counter $7C) or, once the zero byte after record 5 is reached, reloads the slot's own record at $366A.

A 256-byte lookup indexed by screen character value: entry N is the colour-RAM byte for character N. After $6D17 draws the 20-by-10 metatile map window, it jumps to $6F3E, whose loop at $6F59–$6F5F reads each character of that screen buffer and writes the corresponding table byte to colour RAM, 39 columns by 20 rows from $D8C8. The view-shift routines read the table the same way for the column or row a scroll exposes: $30E1 for the right column, $319C for the left column, $3256 for the bottom row and $3314 for the top row. The visual-selector screens take their colours from the tables at $7F9E/$7FA5 instead, through $70ED. The table continues across $8000.
Continuation of the character-to-colour lookup beginning at $7FCF; this byte is entry $31 of that table, and entries continue through $80CE.

A 256-byte attribute table indexed by the map's metatile value. The player's downward check tests bits 0–1 at $0C57 and, for the next column, at $0C7A; the player's horizontal checks at $0EB8 and $1051 test bit 1 when clipping the player against a tile. For entities, the downward scan at $450C tests bits 0–1 at $4532 and $4542, and the horizontal test at $460C reads four attributes through $4632 (at $464C), keeping bit 1 of the first two and bit 0 of the last two.

A 256-byte table of top-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D4D writes the selected code to the first cell of a two-by-two screen block. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of top-right character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D53 writes the selected code to the cell to the right of the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($58) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and ($5A) at $2EF0 (down) and $2FCB (up), for a row of top halves.

A 256-byte table of bottom-left character codes indexed by a metatile value. The full-screen draw loop at $6D5A writes the selected code to one 40-character screen row below the first cell. The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2D02 (scrolling right) and $2DF7 (left), for a column of left halves, and ($58) at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

The scroll routines $2C8D, $2D82, $2E77 and $2F45 read it through a pointer when they draw a newly exposed column or row: they point ($5A) at $2CF1 (scrolling right) and $2DE6 (left), for a column of right halves, and at $2EDF (down) and $2FBA (up), for a row of bottom halves.

Load 15: characters $80–$E1 of the map's character set, the eight-page copy that starts at $8DA6 (the source address at $7F41/$7F42), 784 bytes. $717C copies them to $D400–$D70F. The map's tiles draw characters $83–$89, $90–$9F, $B2–$B3, $B6–$B9, $BB–$C0 and $E1.

Load 15 update entry: load X from $4DBD and write $05, the round number, to $4DCB,X. It jumps to $0732, which loads the next part, when row $6F3D equals $0E and column $6F3C equals $38; otherwise it jumps to $0200. The eight-page character copy from $7F41, which starts at $8DA6, also takes these bytes from $D710 on, as characters $E2–$E5; none of the load's four metatile corner tables names them.

Load 15 trigger record 1 of 2: initial bytes $17, $0B, $01, $FF, $DE, $94. $7979 copies the fields to the column, row, remaining-count, argument and callback arrays; the initial callback address is $94DE. $48BF compares the stored column and row with the view tile, checks and decrements the count, then dispatches through the callback. The callback $94DE leaves the count alone, and apart from $7979 and the dispatcher no other code writes it, so the record fires once.

Load 15 trigger record 2 of 2: initial bytes $3C, $09, $01, $05, $2A, $5C. $7979 copies the fields to the column, row, remaining-count, argument and callback arrays; the initial callback address is $5C2A. $48BF compares the stored column and row with the view tile, checks and decrements the count, then dispatches through the callback. The callback $5C2A places a hidden coin, entity type $FD drawn with sprite $99, in entity slot zero at the record's tile ($5D2C) with the argument $05 as its reward byte; when slot zero is occupied it adds one back to the count instead ($5C30), so the record fires again on a later pass. Apart from $7979 and the dispatcher, no other code writes the count.

Load 15: a map-trigger callback. Trigger record 1 at $94D2 (column $17, row $0B, count 1, argument $FF) names it, and $48BF calls it with the trigger index in X. It saves X in the operand of the LDX at $94E8, loads message pointer $94EB (“THE MAM DESERT.”) in X/Y and calls $77E0 at $94E5; $94E8 then restores X and $94EA returns. The map's character copy, which starts at $8DA6, also takes $94DE–$94E5 to $D738–$D73F as character $E7.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “THE MAM DESERT.” / “”, then the control byte $18. The instruction sequence at $94E1 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 24 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 15 stage-object record 1 of 1: bytes $08, $09, $01, $05, $46, $95, $11, $95, $10, $05, $72, $95, $82, $83, $84, $85. $4655 copies bytes 0–11 to the twelve arrays at $4747–$4789 (bytes 0–3 are the column, row, screen selector and state) and bytes 12–15 to $7D–$80, then calls $46D6, which writes those four map cells as the two-by-two block at columns $08–$09 of rows $08–$09; when the state byte is negative it first replaces them with $7F6D–$7F70, or $7F71–$7F74 when $7A is nonzero. When the main loop’s call of $478F at $042C finds the hero at column $08, row $09 ($6F3C/$6F3D) with $527D equal to $0F, the input byte $75 zero and the state not negative, $479C lowers the state ($05 at the start) by 2, passes byte 2, $01, in X to $7119 at $47F5, which draws the screen of visual selector 1, and calls the callback $9572 from bytes 10 and 11 through the JSR at $47FC; if the state is then negative, $46D6 rewrites the cells.

Stage-object record 1 at $9501 holds this address in bytes 6–7 and names the shop's price set-up $9572 as its callback. When the player pays the first price, $9654–$9667 patches this address into the JSR at $9667, clears its high byte at $9664 so that it runs once, and calls it. Tail-jump to $77E0 with message $9518 (“When you fight the / Dragon, aim at / its head.[$60]”, control byte $FF, so it waits for Fire).

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “When you fight the” / “Dragon, aim at” / “its head.[$60]”, then the control byte $FF. [$60] is glyph $60, the downward-pointing triangle that ends a page. The instruction sequence at $9511 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B; for $FF it shows the message on the status panel through two calls of $370B, waits for Fire at $6DDE, which blinks the triangle, and then sets the countdown to 5, so the message stays for five more panel updates.

Load 15: a message callback; stage-object record 1 at $9501 names it in its bytes 4 and 5. It shows message $954D (“The pyramid is” …) through $77E0. The map's eight-page character copy, which starts at $8DA6, also takes $9546–$954C to $D7A0–$D7A6 as character $F4.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “The pyramid is” / “said to have” / “a bar.[$60]”, then the control byte $FF. [$60] is glyph $60, the downward-pointing triangle that ends a page. The instruction sequence at $9546 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B; for $FF it shows the message on the status panel through two calls of $370B, waits for Fire at $6DDE, which blinks the triangle, and then sets the countdown to 5, so the message stays for five more panel updates.

Two jump entries: $9572 enters the price setup at $9578, and $9575 jumps to the item-pair setup at $9698. Load 15’s stage-object record 1 at $9501 names $9572 as its callback; no record or instruction in load 15 or in the resident part names $9575. The map’s eight-page character copy, which starts at $8DA6, also takes these six bytes, to $D7CC–$D7D1.

Write $46 plus 1 modulo 256 to the high address byte at $98D7 of the digit store at $98D5 and to the layout gate at $9921, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and use stage index $7B to format fields $4783,X and $4789,X through $95DB with Y=$9B and Y=$AF as the screen offsets of their last digits.
Use selected-player index $4DBD. If $4DC7,Y is nonzero, or if $4DC9,Y is at least stage field $4789,X under an unsigned byte comparison, go to $95C6. Otherwise inspect stage field $4753,X.

Branch to $95C6 if the preceding balance comparison has carry set. Otherwise reload record index X from $7B, compare field $4753,X with 3, and branch to $95B8 when unequal; equality falls through to its fixed-message path.
Reached when stage field $4753,X is 3 or has bit 0 clear: select message $9A10 and jump to the message call at $9862.

Reached when stage field $4753,X is not 3: test its bit 0. A clear bit selects message $9A10; a set bit calls $98A9, which stores $FF in $4753,X, then selects message $99FA and jumps to the message call at $9862.

Reached from the balance check when the gold covers stage field $4789,X. Test bit 0 of stage field $4753,X: clear selects message $99BC, set selects $99A5. Both jump to $9755, which shows the message and starts the choice loop.

Save X in the immediate operand at $9603 and Y in the one at $95FE, call $36E9 to split A into nibbles plus one, clear the first two bytes at $991C, and write the tens and units codes to the next two bytes. A tens code of 1 is written as zero. Restore Y, call $98C3, restore X and return.

The flags come from the selection byte $9922, loaded at $97EE before the only jump here ($97F1, taken when the layout gate $9921 is nonzero): negative ($FF, left) enters the first-price balance check at $9637; zero selects message $99E3 at $9685; otherwise (1, right) take the second-price path at $9609.

Reached from $9605 when the shop selection byte is 1. Load X from $7B and call $78D1 with stage field $4789,X, record byte 9, the second price: $78D1 subtracts it in packed decimal from the selected player’s gold and restores the gold if that borrows. Reload X and read callback high byte $4771,X. If nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9627 from $476B/$4771 (record bytes 4 and 5), clear the high byte in the stage record so that the callback runs only once, and call the patched target; then use A=4 at $967A, which adds it to the life meter. If zero, enter the message path at $962E, which shows message $9A51 and then does the same with A=4. In load 15, stage record 1 at $9501 names this shop’s entry $9572, with second price $05 and callback $9546.

Second-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9A51 (“Nice and cold, / is'nt it?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=4 and jump to $9675, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 4 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9616 branches here when the callback high byte $4771,X (record byte 5) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the second price, record byte 9, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. In load 15 stage-object record 1 at $9501 names the price set-up $9572 as its callback.

If selected-player high balance $4DC7,Y is zero and low balance $4DC9,Y is less than stage field $4783,X under an unsigned byte comparison, jump to $9775. Otherwise continue to the first-price payment at $964C.

Reached from the balance check at $9637, which the selection path sends here when the shop selection byte is $FF and lets through when the selected player’s gold covers the first price. Call $78D1 with stage field $4783,X, record byte 8, the first price, which $78D1 subtracts in packed decimal from the gold, and reload the stage index. If callback high byte $477D,X is nonzero, patch the JSR operand at $9668 from $4777/$477D (record bytes 6 and 7), clear that high byte so that the callback runs only once, and call the target; then use A=8 at $967A, which adds it to the life meter. Otherwise enter the message path at $966F, which shows message $9A6C and then does the same with A=8. In load 15, stage record 1 at $9501 names this shop’s entry $9572, with first price $10 and callback $9511.

First-price fallback: load X/Y with message $9A6C (“How do you like / the cocktail?”, control byte $10, so the panel shows it for 16 updates), set A=8 and fall into $9675, which calls $77E0, pulls A and adds 8 to the selected player's life meter through $77A9. $9657 branches here when the callback high byte $477D,X (record byte 7) is zero, after $78D1 has taken the first price, record byte 8, from the gold; the high byte is cleared once that record's callback has run. In load 15 stage-object record 1 at $9501 names the price set-up $9572 as its callback.

Push A, call $77E0 with the message pointer in X/Y and pull A, then continue at $967A, which adds A to the player’s meter through $77A9. The second-price fallback jumps here from $9634 with A=4 and message $9A51; the first-price fallback falls in from $966F with A=8 and message $9A6C.

Call $77A9 with A=4 or A=8, reload stage index, decrement $4753,X and jump to $9865. The two price paths jump here, $962B with A=4 and $966C with A=8, after paying. $77A9 adds A to the selected player’s life meter $4DCD,Y, capped at the limit $4DCF,Y; $9865 calls $3C2A and $370B until the message countdown $4D6B is zero and returns. In load 15 stage record $9501 names this shop’s entry.
Load X/Y with message pointer $99E3 and jump to the message call at $9862. $9607 branches here when the selection byte read at $97EE is zero.

Reload stage index, decrement $4753,X, load message pointer $9A2D in X/Y and jump to the message call at $9862. The only jump here is from the timeout path at $979A, taken when the layout gate $9921 is nonzero.
Store zero at the layout gate $9921, set sound state $2C15 to 2, and set $4D69 to 7. Reload stage index from $7B and continue to the item-pair selection at $96A9. The jump entry at $9575 leads here.

Read $476B,X. If nonzero, pass it and $4771,X separately through the conditional-item resolver at $9871; store the returned values at $9927/$9928, then jump to $96E6. If zero, branch to the implicit pair at $96C2.

Use $4771,X, byte 5 of the stage-object record selected by $7B, as Y. Clear carry, add the selected player $4DBD (0 or 1) and then $D5, and store the sum as the low byte of the LDA at $96D6; store $4D plus the carry as its high byte. Load 15 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9575, which leads here; record 1 at $9501 names the price entry at $9572.

Read the absolute address patched by $96CC and $96D3, $4DD5 plus stage field $4771,X plus the selected player index; clear carry and add $9929,Y, where Y is that stage field. Store the result at $9927, then store that result plus one modulo 256 at $9928. Continue at $96E6.

Load the second item's number from $9928, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and read the picture-routine address at offsets 2 and 3 of its row in the 24-row item table at $9C78. Patch the JSR operand at $96FC/$96FD. Load 15 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9575; record 1 at $9501 names the price entry at $9572.

Multiply A, the second item's number that $96E6 loads from $9928, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9C7A,Y and $9C7B,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $96FB, which calls it with A=$E4. No stage record in load 15 names the item-shop entry $9575, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $9698, so this code does not run in load 15.
Call the patched target with A=$E4. Then read the first item byte at $9927, multiply it by eight modulo 256 and patch the JSR operand at $9714/$9715 from the same pointer table.

Multiply A, the first item's number that $96FE loads from $9927, by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's picture-routine address at $9C7A,Y and $9C7B,Y (row offsets 2 and 3) into the operand of the JSR at $9713, which calls it with A=$D0. No stage record in load 15 names the item-shop entry $9575, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $9698, so this code does not run in load 15.
Call the second patched target with A=$D0, then set the temporary row counter at $9C77 to 3 and begin filling colour RAM.

For each of three rows, write colour 9 to four bytes at $D8F8,Y and four at $D90C,Y. Y starts at zero and advances by 40 after each row; the counter at $9C77 ends at zero. With I/O visible, these are colour RAM writes. The next setup continues at $9735.
Store $46 plus one modulo 256 at $98D7. Pass the first selected item at $9927 to $98DE, then call $98C3 with Y=$73. Repeat for the second item at $9928 with Y=$87.

Call $77E0 with the message pointer selected by the preceding path, then fall through to the mode and countdown initializer at $9758. The item-pair path loads $992E; the price path jumps here from $95D1 or $95D8 with $99BC or $99A5.

Store 0 in the selection byte at $9922, store $DC in the countdown at $9926, and fall through to the wait path at $9762. Besides this store, only the left and right handlers write the selection byte, and they keep it among $FF, 0 and 1.

Call $3C2A, decrement the shop countdown at $9926 and branch to $9795 when it becomes zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9899 and $9886; on set carry, repeat this path. On clear carry, fall through to $9775. Starting from the initialized $DC, the countdown reaches zero on the 220th call to $3C2A, counting the calls of this loop and of the one at $9775 together.
Call $3C2A, decrement $9926 and branch to $9795 at zero. Otherwise call $370B, $9899 and $3C4C, then fall through to the sampled-input choice at $9786.

Use the sampled active-low inputs: if $70 is zero, branch to the shop gate at $97E9; otherwise, if $73 is zero, branch to the left handler at $97AB; otherwise, if $74 is zero, branch to the right handler at $97C9. When all three are nonzero, jump back to $9775. The preceding code calls $3C4C to sample joystick port 2; fire takes priority over left, and left over right.

Reached when the countdown at $9926 reaches zero. If $9921 is nonzero, jump to $968C. Otherwise load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X, load X/Y with message pointer $9963, and jump to the $77E0 call at $9862.

If the signed mode byte at $9922 is negative, return to the wait path at $9762. Otherwise decrement it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9921 is zero, pass the item index at $9927 to the message selector at $98B1. Call $9899 and return to the wait path.

If the mode byte at $9922 equals 1, return to the wait path at $9762. Otherwise increment it with eight-bit wrap. If the new value is nonzero and $9921 is zero, pass the item index at $9928 to the message selector at $98B1. Call $9899 and return to the wait path.

Read the layout gate $9921; if nonzero, load the selection byte $9922 and jump to $9605. Otherwise load X from $7B and read $9922. If nonzero, branch to the purchase index choice at $9812, preserving the negative flag from that read. If zero, inspect $4753,X: a negative value or a clear bit 1 selects message pointer $998B; a nonnegative value with bit 1 set selects $9974. Both paths jump to the $77E0 message call. $9921 is $46 plus one on the price path ($957E) and zero on the item-pair path ($969A).
Choose an item index using the incoming negative flag: load $9927 when it is set, or $9928 when clear, then enter the price selector at $981D. The path at $97E9 supplies that flag from $9922.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts, use the result as Y, and copy the item row's price at $9C78,Y and $9C79,Y (row offsets 0 and 1) to $7D/$7E. Call $7901, which subtracts the packed-decimal amount from the selected player’s gold, restores it on insufficient funds, returns carry set on success and clears decimal mode. The code at $9812 passes the first item's number from $9927 when the selection byte is negative, or the second item's from $9928. No stage record in load 15 names the item-shop entry $9575, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $9698, so this code does not run in load 15.

After the $7901 price subtraction, jump to $9762 on clear carry. On set carry, load X from $7B and decrement $4753,X with eight-bit wrap. Read $9922; if negative select the item index at $9927, otherwise select $9928. Push it and continue to the offset-4 routine-pointer selector at $9847.

Multiply A by 8 with three eight-bit shifts and use the result as Y. Copy the item row's purchase-routine address at $9C7C,Y and $9C7D,Y (row offsets 4 and 5) into the operand of the JSR at $985B, which calls it with the item number plus 1 in A. A is the bought item's number, pushed by the code before: the first item from $9927 when the selection byte is negative, otherwise the second from $9928. No stage record in load 15 names the item-shop entry $9575, which jumps to the item-pair selection at $9698, so this code does not run in load 15.

Pull the selected item index, clear carry, add 1 in binary mode and call the JSR whose operand was patched by the selector. Load X/Y with $9950 and call $77E0, then call $3C2A and $370B repeatedly while $4D6B is nonzero. Return once it is zero.
Load 15: return A unchanged unless it equals $13. For $13, inspect bit $10 of the selected player’s flags: return $14 when set, or $13 when clear. The shop item-pair path uses this resolver.

Load 15: call the input sampler at $3C4C and return carry set if any of $73, $74 or $70 is zero, carry clear if all are nonzero. The sampler reads joystick port 2 active-low, so carry is set while the stick is pushed left or right or fire is pressed.

Load 15: with decimal mode clear, add one to the selection byte at $9922, use the wrapped result as an index into $9923, and pass that position in X and $82 in Y to $719E. The selection byte stays among $FF, 0 and 1, so the index is 0 to 2.
Load X from $7B, store $FF at $4753,X and return. The insufficient-gold path calls it at $95BC, and the item effects at $9D3B, $9D41, $9D47, $9D4D, $9D56, $9D62 and $9D7F tail-call it.

Multiply A, an item's number, by 8 using three eight-bit shifts, clear carry, add 6 and use the eight-bit result as X. Read the high byte from $9C79,X into Y and the low byte from $9C78,X into X, the message pointer at offsets 6 and 7 of the item's row in the 24-row item table at $9C78, then jump to $77E0. Entry $77E0 loads A=0, so the message routine uses X/Y as a direct pointer. The selection paths call this routine at $97C0 with the first item's number from $9927 and at $97E0 with the second's from $9928. Load 15 never runs it: no stage-object record names the shop's item-pair entry at $9575; record 1 at $9501 names the price entry at $9572.

Load 15: process four price-display bytes at $991C in reverse order. Leave zero unchanged; add $F5 to each nonzero byte with eight-bit wrap and decimal mode clear. Call the digit writer at $98D5 with successive Y positions, decrementing Y after each call.

Load 15: store A at offset Y of the page after $46, through STA $FF00,Y. $957B and $9738 each set its high byte $98D7 to $46 plus one, $C1 or $C5, since $46 holds the screen page $C0 or $C4; the load holds $FF there. Then write colour 1 to $D900,Y, the matching colour RAM, and return. Called from $98CD. Colour RAM requires I/O visible.

Load 15: multiply item ID A by eight with eight-bit wrap, split the two packed bytes from the item table at $9C78 into four nibble-plus-one values at $991C, and replace consecutive leading ones with zero. It never runs in load 15: its callers at $973E and $9749 are reached only from the item-pair entry $9575, and the load's only shop record, stage record 0, names the price entry $9572 instead.

Load 15: four working price-display bytes. The item-price formatter at $98DE and the stage-price formatter at $95DB write them, and the drawing loop at $98C3 reads them in reverse, from $991F down to $991C, passing each to the digit writer at $98D5.

Load 15: one byte, $A0 in the load, between the four price-display cells at $991C–$991F and the layout gate at $9921. No instruction in load 15 or in the resident part names it, and the indexed accesses to $991C at $98C5, $990C and $9913 keep X between 0 and 3, so none reaches it.
Load 15: mutable shop layout gate. Timeout, selection and purchase code read this byte to choose alternate paths.
Load 15: mutable shop selection byte. The input loop initializes it to zero, left and right paths update it, and the cursor helper indexes the position table using this value plus one.

Load 15: three cursor-position bytes, $5F, $B4 and $FF, for selections $FF, 0 and 1: the cursor helper at $9899 reads them at $98A2 with the selection byte plus one as index, and passes the byte in X to $719E. No instruction writes them.
Load 15: mutable shop timeout. The input loop initializes it to $DC and decrements it during both input-release and polling paths.

Load 15: mutable first item ID. $96B3 or $96DD stores it; the item drawing at $96FE, the price label at $973B, the left-selection description at $97BD and the purchase paths at $981A and $9843 read it.

Load 15: mutable second item ID. $96BC or $96E3 stores it; the item drawing at $96E6, the price label at $9746, the right-selection description at $97DD and the purchase paths at $9814 and $983D read it.

Load 15: five item-index offsets, $00, $00, $0D, $00 and $06, at $9929–$992D. ADC $9929,Y at $96DA adds the selected offset to the player-state value and stores the first item ID; the following addition of one supplies the second ID, with Y equal to stage field $4771,X. Load 15 never reads them: its only stage record, record 1 at $9501, names the price entry $9572, and nothing names the item-pair entry $9575.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “Welcome!” / “May I help you?” / “”, then the control byte $20. The instruction sequence at $9751 loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 32 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Three zero-terminated glyph lines, with alignment spaces omitted here: “” / “Thank you.” / “”, then the control byte $10. The instruction sequence at $985E loads this address in X/Y and passes it to $77E0, which loads A with 0 and so copies the lines into the three message buffers. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B, so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 15, shop message 3: three zero-terminated fields "" / "      Closed." / "", followed by control byte $18. The shop timeout at $9795, when the layout gate $9921 is zero, stores $FF in stage field $4753,X and loads this address in X/Y at $97A4, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $9862. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 24 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 15, shop message 4: three zero-terminated fields "" / " Please come again." / "", followed by control byte $10. The purchase gate at $97E9 loads this address in X/Y at $980B when the selection byte is zero and stage field $4753,X is not negative and has bit 1 set, then jumps to the $77E0 call at $9862. $77E2 stores the control byte in the message countdown $4D6B ($7845), so the status panel shows the message for 16 of its updates ($3719, which runs on every second call of $370B, counts it down) and then redraws the status.

Load 15, shop message 5: three zero-terminated fields "Oh, he's" / "just browsing." / "", followed by control byte $10. Forty signed movement values: $FD, $FE, $FF, 0, 1, 2, 3, thirteen 4s, 3, 2, 1, 0, $FF, $FE, $FD and thirteen $FC values. State 1 returns to state 0 when $1A8F,X is zero. Otherwise clear $1AD3,X. If $1AC2,X is negative, call $45BC with A=8 and set $19C3,X to $19E5,X plus $10 with carry clear.
